title: Why You Feel Cold When You Are Scared
hook: Fear can make your body feel suddenly much colder.

narration.text: Fear can make your body feel suddenly much colder.
This quick temperature drop is a survival mechanism.
Your brain senses danger and triggers a 'fight or flight' response.
Blood rushes away from your skin and towards your muscles.
This prepares your limbs for action, but leaves your skin cool.
It can also reduce blood loss from potential injuries.
So, that chill is your body readying itself for an escape.
Have you noticed this cold sensation during a scary moment?

description: Ever wondered why a sudden fright can give you the chills? It's your body's ancient survival mechanism kicking in. Learn how the 'fight or flight' response impacts your body temperature.
topic: Why you might feel a sudden drop in temperature when you are scared, explaining the physiological response to fear.
